article.title: NFL EDGE Friday Morning Brief
article.dek: The Bears won Thursday night but may have lost Cole Kmet, two quarterback situations are moving faster than the app, and the full Sunday board is already live.

items.headline: Bears 30, Patriots 24 — and Kmet goes down
paragraphs: Chicago held off New England 30-24 on Thursday night to move to 5-2. Cairo Santos drilled a career-long 58-yard field goal with 1:34 left to make it a two-score game, and the Bears recovered the onside kick to close it. Caleb Williams went 22-of-33 for 308 yards and two touchdowns; Drake Maye answered with 321 yards, two touchdowns, an interception, and a rushing score.

The win came at a cost. Tight end Cole Kmet was carted off with a right knee injury with 5:46 left in the fourth quarter and was ruled out for the game. Coach Ben Johnson: "I don't think it looked very good." The Bears run more tests Friday.
The -3 the board held all day covered. There is nothing left to Check on this one — settle it in the tracker honestly, whichever side you had.
items.takeaway: Bears 5-2, Patriots 4-3 — and all eyes on Kmet's Friday test results before next week's board.

items.headline: Quarterback watch: McCarthy in, Lamar day-to-day, McKee again
paragraphs: J.J. McCarthy will start for the Giants on Sunday at Houston, coach John Harbaugh announced Wednesday, and McCarthy took the first-team reps Thursday. He replaces the benched Jameis Winston.

Lamar Jackson practiced on a limited basis Wednesday and again Thursday — the second straight day — moving well without favoring the sprained ankle. He is day-to-day and coach Jesse Minter has not confirmed the starter for Sunday's home game against Cincinnati.

Two of these three are moving faster than the app. The board still lists Jameis Winston for the Giants and Tyler Huntley for the Ravens — it has not caught up to either story. Tanner McKee's second straight start Monday is the one the app already has right.
items.takeaway: Inactives become official about 90 minutes before kickoff Sunday — until then, treat the QB rows on the board as stale and run your price through Check.

items.headline: Simmons to IR, Jacobs back, Paris game still on
paragraphs: Chiefs left tackle Josh Simmons (back/bulging disc) went on injured reserve Thursday after his rehab 'plateaued' — out at least four more games, no surgery planned. Undrafted rookie Kahlil Benson keeps the job. The 5-0 Chiefs visit Seattle on Sunday night.
Josh Jacobs is back at Packers practice and is expected to play this week, per NFL Network, after being cleared following the league's investigation. Green Bay visits Detroit on Sunday.
Pittsburgh canceled a planned Paris fan event over security concerns tied to civil unrest in France. Sunday's Steelers-Saints game — 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff — remains scheduled.
items.takeaway: Line-protection news for Sunday night, a lead back returning for Sunday afternoon, and logistics noise (not a postponement) in Paris.

items.headline: Weather: nothing today
paragraphs: No NFL games today, so no kickoff windows to check. Sunday's outdoor forecasts firm up closer to Sunday — the Sunday editions will carry the final kickoff-window weather.
items.takeaway: Friday is a weather off-day; check back Sunday morning before you lock anything in.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: Your three cards this morning
paragraphs: Hit Rate: Vikings moneyline at -278 on DraftKings — the pick the app thinks is most likely to win. Hit Rate forgoes value for win probability; the app's own tutorial says Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
Balanced: Browns moneyline at -126 on FanDuel — the middle ground, a strong pick without paying too much. A fine starting point if you are new to this.
Value: Buccaneers +3 at -105 on DraftKings — always the model's +EV play. The price ticked a nickel worse overnight (was +100) and it is still the card.
None of these is a command. They are the three lanes the app sees; your price, through Check, decides whether any of them is a bet.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate = most likely to win. Balanced = strong without overpaying. Value = the +EV play. Check = the verdict on your price.

items.headline: Monday night: the model and the market disagree
paragraphs: The model's expected margin has Cowboys-Eagles at about a pick'em. The market board has Dallas -4.5 at both DraftKings and FanDuel. That is a wide gap, and it is not a typo — the market has Tanner McKee's second start and a four-game Eagles losing streak fully priced in.

A gap like this does not mean the model is wrong or the market is wrong. It means this is exactly the spot Check was built for: type in your book's line and price on Monday night, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and hands you a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your number — not the board's, not anyone else's.
items.takeaway: When the model says pick'em and the market says -4.5, don't guess — Check your price. Monday game? Monday check.

items.headline: Two boards built on yesterday's quarterbacks
paragraphs: The Giants board was built on Jameis Winston. The starter Sunday is J.J. McCarthy. The Ravens board was built on Tyler Huntley. The starter Sunday might be Lamar Jackson — or might still be Huntley. The app has not caught up to either story.

This is the one timing note that matters today: inactives become official about 90 minutes before kickoff Sunday. That is when these two games get real. Until then, any number you liked on Giants-Texans or Bengals-Ravens was priced for a quarterback who may not play — run it through Check, and be ready to re-run it when the starters are official.
items.takeaway: Stale QB rows + fresh prices = Check now, Check again when inactives drop about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Learn the Game: handle vs. tickets
paragraphs: Two numbers you will see on any betting-splits page: BET is the share of tickets (how many bets), HND is the share of handle (how much money). Tickets count heads. Handle counts dollars.

A concrete, clearly-labeled hypothetical: say 70% of the tickets are on the favorite, but 60% of the money is on the underdog. The crowd is loud and the money is quiet — most bettors took the favorite, but the bigger dollars took the dog. That disagreement between tickets and handle is what bettors call a split.

A split is not a command to bet the other side. It is a question: why does the money disagree with the crowd? Sometimes the answer is nothing. Sometimes it is information you do not have yet. Either way, you now know what to watch — the line. If the line starts moving toward the money side, the market is telling you something.
This morning the free splits row showed no data for Thursday's game, so there is no real split to work with — which is exactly why this space is a lesson instead of a manufactured Fade.
items.takeaway: Tickets count heads, handle counts dollars — when they disagree, watch the line, not the crowd, and never force a Fade that isn't there.

items.headline: Overnight: one half-point, two price ticks
paragraphs: The only real move since the evening board: the Steelers-Saints game ticked a half point at DraftKings, Saints +3.5 to +3.0 — money toward New Orleans. FanDuel never moved off +3.0.

Two price ticks on the cards: the Value play (Buccaneers +3) got a nickel worse, +100 to -105 at DraftKings — still the card. The Hit Rate play (Vikings moneyline) got a tick better, -285 to -278. The Balanced card (Browns -126) never moved. Everything else on the Sunday board was flat.

The board refreshed this morning and refreshes again tonight. If your book isn't DK or FanDuel, the drill never changes: tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator for a bet-or-no-bet verdict on your price. Full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
items.takeaway: Quiet night: one half-point (toward New Orleans), one cheaper Hit Rate, one pricier Value play — and the board caught all of it.

items.headline: Opener vs. now: the week's two big moves
paragraphs: From the shadow-tracked lookahead lines published October 15 to this morning's board, the two biggest moves of the week: Raiders +7.0 down to +3.5 against the Rams — three and a half points toward Las Vegas — and Texans -7.0 out to -10.5 against the Giants, as the McCarthy news landed during the week.
The closed one: Patriots-Bears opened Bears -1.5, closed -3, and finished 30-24 — the move and the result agreed.
Moves usually mean something, even when the reason isn't obvious yet. When you see one, the question is always the same: is there news behind it, or is it just money?
items.takeaway: Raiders +7 to +3.5 and Texans -7 to -10.5 were the week's big movers — both had real news behind them.

items.headline: Friday is for the Sunday board
paragraphs: No games today. The whole Sunday board is live right now — thirteen games, lines and prices, all three cards. The most useful thing you can do with a football Friday is run the prices you actually like through Check today, before the weekend moves the numbers on you.

And the standing nudge, because settlement is manual and the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself: log last night's result — winner or loser, whichever side you had. The tracker can't teach you anything from games you pretend didn't happen.
items.takeaway: Check your Sunday prices today, and log Thursday's result honestly — the tracker only works if you do.
